title: Eliminate chronic subjective tinnitus after a finite treatment

concept.text: Produce sustained disappearance of chronic tinnitus percepts after treatment ends. Existing management can reduce distress and severity; neither NIH nor WHO identifies a definitive cure. Proposed completion test: Regulatory authorization supported by an adequately powered sham-controlled trial in chronic subjective tinnitus, showing a significantly higher complete-remission rate than control, maintained for at least 12 months after treatment ends, with no continuing masking or stimulation. Test set by: Proposed editorial test; no externally standardized cure threshold was identified. WHO distinguishes the tinnitus percept from tinnitus disorder and associated suffering. Overlaps: PSY-07. Sources given: [NIDCD tinnitus evidence and treatment overview](https://www.nidcd.nih.gov/health/tinnitus) ; [WHO tinnitus questions and answers](https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/deafness-and-hearing-loss--tinnitus).

page.title: Treatment-free remission of chronic subjective tinnitus
page.definition: A finite treatment causes sustained disappearance of tinnitus: sound heard only by the affected person without an external source, persisting for more than 3 months. The sound remains absent after treatment ends, including in silence while deliberately listening for it.

goal.need: A 2022 meta-analysis identified 113 eligible articles and estimated chronic tinnitus prevalence at 9.8% of adults (95% CI, 4.7%–19.3%). Its global estimates for any and severe tinnitus are shown below; these broader categories are not counts of chronic subjective tinnitus. WHO states that no definitive cure exists.

completion.title: A finite treatment increases total tinnitus remission lasting over 6 months after treatment ends.
completion.criterion: In adults with subjective tinnitus lasting more than 3 months, a finite treatment produces a statistically higher rate than sham/placebo of total remission lasting more than 6 months after tinnitus-directed treatment ends. Total remission means no tinnitus perception even in silence with deliberate attention, without masking or continuing stimulation. A preregistered, adequately powered, blinded randomized trial meets its prespecified superiority test and documents adverse events.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis; no generally accepted test of treatment-free perceptual cure was located.
completion.basis: Searched WHO and NIDCD guidance, ATA’s roadmap, FDA’s Lenire order, AAO-HNSF research recommendations, and registered-trial reports; no common treatment-free cure test was found. This combines Sanchez et al.’s remission definition with AAO-HNSF’s controlled-trial requirements. The six-month interval is study-specific, not a consensus cure standard. FDA’s Lenire order concerns temporary symptom relief.

milestones.title: A finite treatment reverses a rat tinnitus proxy through 3 weeks after treatment ends.
milestones.criterion: In the Engineer et al. protocol, restore inhibition of the acoustic startle response by silent gaps in background sound, including at the presumed tinnitus frequency. Cued versus uncued responses meet P < 0.05; restored gap detection persists 1 day, 1 week and 3 weeks after an 18-day course. The 2011 study reported reversal in 7 rats receiving paired tones and vagus-nerve stimulation, versus persistent impairment in 9 sham-treated rats. Gap detection is a behavioral proxy; it cannot establish a rat’s subjective perception.
milestones.set_by: Engineer et al., University of Texas at Dallas and MicroTransponder; published noise-exposed-rat experimental protocol, not a clinical cure standard.
milestones.threshold_quote: the impairment in gap detection was also eliminated when measured one day, one week and three weeks after the end of the therapy.

milestones.title: A controlled human trial shows reduced tinnitus loudness during a 4-week treatment course.
milestones.criterion: The Marks et al. protocol tests weekly tinnitus loudness matching during 28 days of paired sound and skin electrical stimulation against sound-only sham in a double-blind randomized crossover trial, using P < 0.05. In 2018, 20 adults with somatic tinnitus completed the trial; the average loudness-match reduction reached 12.2 dB in week 4. Two reported elimination near the end of active treatment. Loudness reduction did not persist through washout. Somatic tinnitus changes with head or neck movement or pressure.
milestones.set_by: Marks et al., University of Michigan; published human proof-of-concept protocol, restricted to somatic tinnitus.
milestones.threshold_quote: The active bimodal treatment produced a significant (P<0.05) cumulative decrease in tinnitus loudness

milestones.title: A controlled trial finds reduced tinnitus loudness 6 weeks after a 6-week treatment course.
milestones.criterion: The Jones et al. protocol measures loudness at weeks 6 and 12 after 30 minutes/day of paired sound and skin electrical stimulation for 6 weeks, followed by 6 weeks without treatment, against an auditory-only control; two-sided P < 0.05 defines significance. In 2023, 99 adults with somatic tinnitus were randomized. In the active-first group, the intention-to-treat mean change progressed from −5.8 dB sensation level at week 6 to −9.2 dB at week 12. Sensation level is relative to hearing threshold. These are partial reductions.
milestones.set_by: University of Michigan protocol NCT03621735, reported by Jones et al.; restricted to bothersome somatic tinnitus.
milestones.threshold_quote: Primary end points were changes in TFI score and tinnitus loudness level from baseline through week 6 and week 12.

milestones.title: People with daily tinnitus for over 3 months have no tinnitus perception for over 6 months.
milestones.criterion: Apply Sanchez et al.’s inclusion test: previous daily tinnitus for over 3 months, followed by no perception even in silence with deliberate attention for over 6 months; exclude habituation and masking. The 2021 series enrolled 80 people already in remission and scheduled interviews after 6, 12 and 18 months. Selection of remitters without a control group cannot estimate treatment efficacy. In the 2025 MOST trial, 1 of 440 participants reached its different remission endpoint, a zero Tinnitus Handicap Inventory score, at month 6; that handicap endpoint alone does not establish absent perception.
milestones.set_by: Sanchez, Valim and Schlee, published case-collection inclusion protocol; a study-specific definition of total remission, without a requirement establishing treatment causation.
milestones.threshold_quote: total remission (lack of tinnitus perception, even in silence and with deliberate attention to it) for over 6 months.

not_found: No controlled report located demonstrated superiority for total perceptual remission lasting over six months after a finite treatment ended.
Full texts of the 2007 Tinnitus Research Initiative outcome consensus and the international trial-methodology proposal were blocked by access-check pages.

results.finding: In 7 treated rats, gap detection impairment was eliminated through 3 weeks after treatment.
results.detail: After 18 days of paired tones and vagus-nerve stimulation, gap detection was restored at all tested frequencies; 9 sham-treated rats remained impaired. Gap detection is a behavioral proxy and cannot establish subjective perception.
results.quote: In the rats that received VNS paired with multiple tones, the impairment in gap detection was also eliminated when measured one day, one week and three weeks after the end of the therapy.

results.finding: In 20 adults with somatic tinnitus, mean loudness matching decreased by 12.2 dB in week 4 of active treatment.
results.detail: The randomized, double-blind crossover trial compared paired sound and skin electrical stimulation with sound-only sham. The active-treatment reduction was significant at P < 0.05; loudness reduction did not persist into washout. Two participants reported elimination near the end of active treatment.
results.quote: Tinnitus reduction reached an average of 12.2 dB in the fourth week of active treatment. Of the 20 participants tested, two reported complete elimination of their tinnitus towards the end of the active treatment period.

results.finding: In 99 adults with somatic tinnitus, active-first treatment reduced mean tinnitus loudness by 9.2 dB SL at week 12 in the intention-to-treat population.
results.detail: Participants received 6 weeks of active or auditory-only treatment, followed by 6 weeks without treatment. At week 12, the reported intention-to-treat difference between active and control was −4.5 dB SL (P = .001). The result is a reduction, not disappearance of tinnitus.
results.quote: As observed for the TFI scores, there was some tinnitus loudness level decrease during the auditory-only treatment, but the decrease was minimal and significantly less than that during the bisensory treatment.

results.finding: 80 people with prior daily tinnitus reported total remission lasting over 6 months.
results.detail: Participants were selected because they were already in remission; the uncontrolled series cannot establish treatment efficacy.
results.quote: By publishing announcements, we included volunteers of any gender and age who have had daily perception of tinnitus for over 3 months and have been in total remission (lack of tinnitus perception, even in silence and with deliberate attention to it) for over 6 months.
